title: Human-Computer Interaction
description: Principles and methods of interaction design: understanding users, conceptual design, data gathering and analysis, cognition, prototyping and evaluation.

topics.title: HCI, Interactive Systems and Usability
topics.summary: HCI studies how people interact with computers through three entities: the user, the computer and the interaction. Its goal is usable, safe systems that are effective, efficient, learnable, memorable and enjoyable, designed with people first.
subtopics: Interactive systems: past, present and future
Good and poor design
Definition of HCI (ACM) and the disciplines involved
Cultural factors and digital inclusion
Usability goals: effectiveness, efficiency, safety, utility, learnability, memorability
User experience (UX) goals, and HCI versus UX

topics.title: Understanding the Problem Space and User-Centred Design
topics.summary: Understand the problem space before designing any interface, because starting with the interface overlooks usability and the user experience. User-centred design puts users' tasks and goals first, using user profiles, personas and scenarios.
subtopics: Understanding the problem space before designing the interface
Dot voting and the Havanna community case study
Levels of engagement with users
Approaches to interaction design: user-centred, activity-centred, system and genius design
Principles of user-centred design: early focus on users
User profiles, personas and scenarios

topics.title: Conceptual Models, Interaction Types and Ideation
topics.summary: A conceptual model is an agreed, high-level description of how a system works, built from metaphors and the five interaction types. Ideation techniques such as brainstorming and brainwriting generate the ideas, and dot voting selects them.
subtopics: Components of a conceptual model
Interface metaphors
Interaction types: instructing, conversing, manipulating, exploring, responding
Representing a conceptual model: diagrams and storyboards
Ideation and ideation techniques (brainstorming)
Conceptual framework / solution overview and ideation tools

topics.title: Data Gathering and Data Analysis
topics.summary: Data gathering uses interviews, focus groups, questionnaires and observation, with sampling, consent, triangulation and pilot studies. Analysis turns the data into findings with simple statistics, graphs, thematic analysis and inferential tests.
subtopics: Identifying participants: probability and non-probability sampling
Pilot studies and informed consent
Interviews (structured, semi-structured, unstructured), focus groups and data recording
Questionnaires: structure, Likert and semantic differential scales
Direct and indirect observation; choosing and combining techniques
Quantitative and qualitative analysis: percentages, graphs, outliers, thematic analysis
Inferential analysis: dependent and independent variables; Cronbach's alpha

topics.title: Cognitive Psychology and Perception
topics.summary: Cognitive psychology explains how people process information, perceive, attend and remember, so designs can match human abilities. It covers the constructivist and ecological theories of perception, the Gestalt principles and the main cognitive processes.
subtopics: Cognition, perception and why cognitive psychology matters in HCI
The human senses
Visual perception: constructivist and ecological theories
Gestalt principles: common region, figure-ground, continuity, closure, proximity, similarity
Cognitive processes: attention, perception and memory

topics.title: Prototyping, Design Principles and Evaluation
topics.summary: Prototypes range from cheap paper sketches to high-fidelity interactive systems, and evaluation tests them with or without users. It covers formative and summative evaluation, Nielsen's heuristics, Shneiderman's golden rules and usability testing.
subtopics: Low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes: advantages and disadvantages
Why, what, where and when to evaluate
Categories of evaluation by user involvement, setting and control
Heuristic evaluation and Nielsen's heuristics
Shneiderman's eight golden rules of interface design
Usability testing, think aloud, diary studies, field studies and experiments
System Usability Scale (Brooke)
